utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm going to read the summary out in the English language. [In English] Tomislav Savkic was born in Dubnica on January the 1st, 1956, Milici municipality. He completed his primary school in Milici and the secondary grammar school in Vlasenica, and then he went on to graduate from the electrical engineering faculty in Tuzla. He got his first job in 1980 at the secondary school centre in Vlasenica where he worked as a teacher. After serving in the army he started working at the Boksit coal mine in Milici in 1984. He worked in this company until the outbreak of the war in 1992. In early 1992 he was appointed commander of the defence of the Boksit mine and after that he worked as an engineer. On November the 1st, 1992, he was appointed commander of the 1st Infantry Battalion in Milici. He remained in this post until November the 1st, 1993, when he became president of the Milici Municipal Assembly. From then on until the end of the war he did not have any military duties. Tomislav Savkic noticed that inter-ethnic problems began mounting when the breakup of Yugoslavia began, particularly when the nationalist parties were established. The SDA were particularly active in glorifying its own ethnic group and the founding Assemblies of the SDA served as platforms for the outpours of hatred towards Serbs and instances of Serbs being threatened. Many Muslims displayed their national emblems and there were a number of instances where the SDS flag was burnt in a Serbian village by the Muslim extremists. During the foundation Assembly of the SDS Serbs travelling to the meeting were pelted with stones. As the result of the multi-party elections, the SDS and SDA divided the government in Vlasenica evenly; however, problems arose from the beginning as the Muslims and the SDA did not have professionally trained staff and their nominees did not have the required qualifications. However, these appointments were granted. In June 1991 the Muslims, on orders from the leaders of the SDA, attempted to break up the JNA. They were ordered not to send their recruits for compulsory military service or respond to the mobilisations. In one instance members of the SDA pressured the president of the Municipal Assembly to provide buses to take them to where the territorial units had been mobilised as they wished to return the Muslim men home. During this period that the Muslims began to procure weapons with urgency, the Serbian people began to worry. And although the SJB, police station, attempted to do something about this arming, they were unsuccessful in stopping it. At the same the Muslims were forming paramilitary units. Many were sent to Croatia for training and policemen were also sent to create a further fighting force. The Muslims in the paramilitary units began openly carrying automatic weapons. In September 1991 at a rally, Muslims -- the Muslims publicly declared by that they already had 250 soldiers ready for war. In the same month, Muslim paramilitary formations started setting up ambushes on the main road between Milici and Skelani, stopping buses transporting employees to the Boksit mine to work. The Muslims would hold on to the bus and force the workers to continue the rest of the route on foot. Muslim paramilitaries would enter Serbian villages and terrorise the population. The security situation was beginning to slip out of control so night sentries were established to ensure the population's safety. Further, over this period the municipal authorities were losing power as they were not able to agree to many topics with the Muslims and many civilians began leaving the municipality. Towards the end of 1991 a proclamation from the Muslim National Council of BH which declared their intentions to create a Muslim state, Muslim armed forces, education, and administrative organs. To try to stop a war, the Serbian people suggested the formation of the Autonomous District of Birac, which would be a part of BH. This was passed on 26th of December, 1991. The Serbs in the authorities tried in many peaceful ways to agree with the Muslims on all the problems in the attempt to avoid the war. Mr. Tomislav Savkic is not aware of any instructions allegedly issued by Radovan Karadzic to the representatives of municipalities at a meeting held in the Holiday Inn Hotel on 20th of December, 1991, neither is he aware of Variants of Plan A and B. The municipality of Milici was established on 31st of March, 1992. A working group was proposed to draw up an agreement on the division of the municipality. Although an agreement was drawn up the Muslims were ordered to drag their feet with completing to allow as many Muslims to leave Srebrenica [sic] as possible. On 24th of April, 1992, as the situation grew more complicated with the Muslim deputies because less agreements were reached, a Crisis Staff for Vlasenica was established. The task of this Crisis Staff was to monitor closely the newly arisen situation and to issue quickly and efficiently decisions aimed at addressing it. The correct circumstances existed to create the Crisis Staff. The authorities received information that the Muslims were preparing to mount an all-out attack on Vlasenica and therefore Territorial Defence units were sent in to dispel this. Following this, the remaining Muslim population then left the area. A number gathered outside the municipal building and the police station asking to be provided with organised transport. At the same time a large number of Serbian refugees started arriving as they had been expelled from other areas by Muslims. These refugees needed to be housed and the authorities decided that the Serbian refugees should be given temporary accommodation in a T -- in a Territorial Defence building until accommodation could be sorted for them in abandoned houses and flats. This issue was resolved in a few days; however, more Muslims gathered awaiting public transport and therefore a decision was made to house them in the Territorial Defence buildings too. Many Muslims returned to the Territorial Defence building at night as they felt safer there, while during the day they were being in city. When Muslim civilians made requests to be housed or have transport provided, the authorities completed their requests as fully as possible. Muslim paramilitary formations continued to carry out ambushes during May 1992, capturing both drivers and vehicles, killing civilians including women and children. Further, the Muslim forces damaged all electricity power lines, leaving the Milici and Vlasenica without electrical power and also mined bridges and tunnels cutting off Milici and Vlasenica from Drina River and Serbia and the rest of the world. In late 1991 and early 1992, Tomislav Savkic was aware that Muslim extremists repeatedly fired automatic weapons at buses carrying secondary school pupils. The only road that could be used for travel had become unsafe due to the Muslim forces ambushing travellers. These attacks continued into September 1992 killing and wounding civilians and many vehicles were torched. To avoid any further losses and to allow the safe passage for the wounded and the civilians and the military authorities decided that a corridor had to be created. At the same time, the Muslim leadership in Sarajevo launched propaganda claiming that the Republika Srpska army was attacking the town of Cerska and slaughtering civilians. A representative of international forces visited Cerska and saw that this was not the case. Srebrenica and Zepa were declared safe areas to be demilitarised. An attempt was made to demilitarise the area; however, the Muslims had orders to only hand-over their old and faulty weapons. Soon soldiers began carrying weapons publicly and carrying out military training and the UN did not react to ammunition being received by Muslim forces. Soldiers were active even after Srebrenica had been declared a safe area, murdering civilians, ambushing, and looting Serbian property. He was aware that the commanders of the BH Army were preparing to mount fresh combat operations from the safe area of Srebrenica in October 1994. Tomislav Savkic considers that the war the Muslims waged on BH was not defensive but an offensive one. Tomislav Savkic never heard Radovan Karadzic or any other political leader from Pale order the killing or the persecution of Muslims, their detention in a camp or the destruction of their property. He was aware that in the beginning Radovan Karadzic was saying that the Serbs had to try and avoid war in every way and, if it did come to war, great care had to be taken to protect Muslim and Croatian civilians and prisoners of war had to be treated extremely humanely. [Interpretation] I would like to leave my questions for tomorrow, Excellencies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Briefly two matters before we adjourn today. While we appreciate your objections, Ms. Sutherland, Mr. Tieger and Ms. Sutherland, in the future I would prefer to hear the objections as soon as possible instead of just prior to the witness's evidence. So either orally or in writing. If urgent, you can e-mail -- you can give notice through e-mail and then we can discuss during the courtroom. Second, in the week of 18th of March the Chamber is minded to sit from Tuesday to Friday instead of Monday to Thursday, due to some internal matters. So if the parties could inform the Chamber staff through e-mail whether it has any problem. I thank again for the -- thank the staff for their indulgence. And, Mr. Savkic, we'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.
